description: Evals for the iris-development skill: Redis Agent Memory SDK setup and auth, session events vs direct long-term memory writes, idempotent bulk creation, search scoping, and the asynchronous promotion contract. These prompts test product-specific facts (package names, env vars, the 5-minute promotion window, the 100-record bulk cap) that are not inferable without the skill.

evals.name: sdk-setup-and-auth
evals.prompt: We provisioned a memory service in the Redis Cloud console for our agent and I have the API key. Now I need to wire up the Python client - what package do I install, how do I authenticate it, and what config does it expect? Don't want to hardcode secrets.
evals.expected_output: Installs the redis-agent-memory package, constructs AgentMemory, and reads the bearer token from AGENT_MEMORY_API_KEY and the default store from AGENT_MEMORY_STORE_ID rather than hardcoding, pointing at the data-plane URL from the Cloud console.
expectations: The output installs the redis-agent-memory Python package.
The output uses the AgentMemory class as the client.
The output reads the API key from the AGENT_MEMORY_API_KEY environment variable.
The output references the AGENT_MEMORY_STORE_ID environment variable for the default store id.
The output points the client at the memory data-plane URL rather than a standard Redis host and port.
The output does not connect with redis-py or a generic Redis client library for this API.
The output does not hardcode the API key in source.

evals.name: session-events-vs-direct-ltm
evals.prompt: Building a customer-support agent with Redis Agent Memory. For each conversation turn I was planning to summarise it myself with an LLM call and write the summary straight into long-term memory, so search always has good data. Is that the right shape or am I overcomplicating it?
evals.expected_output: Says this is overcomplicated: append each turn as a session event and let the managed background promotion worker extract durable facts into long-term memory, reserving direct long-term writes for facts that come from outside a conversation.
expectations: The output recommends appending each conversation turn as a session event.
The output states that a background promotion worker extracts durable facts into long-term memory automatically.
The output identifies the user's own per-turn LLM summarisation as redundant work or duplicated LLM cost.
The output shows the session event call with session id, actor id, role, and content.
The output explains when a direct long-term memory write is still appropriate, such as facts not originating from a session.
The output does not endorse the per-turn manual summarise-then-write approach as the recommended pattern.

evals.name: async-promotion-contract
evals.prompt: Integration test is red and I can't work out why. It calls addSessionEvent with the user saying they prefer dark mode, gets a 200 back, then immediately calls searchLongTermMemory for 'theme preference' and asserts one result. Gets zero. The same search passes if I run it by hand a bit later. Bug in the SDK?
evals.expected_output: Explains this is the documented asynchronous promotion contract rather than a bug: the event enqueues a fire-and-forget promotion job that is delayed until the end of a 5-minute deduplication window plus the LLM round trip, so the test must poll with a timeout instead of asserting synchronously.
expectations: The output states this is expected behavior rather than an SDK bug.
The output explains that a successful session event only enqueues a background promotion job and does not write long-term memory synchronously.
The output states that promotion is delayed by a deduplication window, identifying it as 5 minutes.
The output tells the user to poll with a timeout instead of asserting immediately after the write.
The output notes that long-term memory is eventually consistent with respect to session events.
The output does not suggest the fix is to retry addSessionEvent or to write the memory directly to work around a defect.

evals.name: bulk-create-idempotency-and-cap
evals.prompt: One-off backfill: I've got roughly 4,000 extracted facts about our users sitting in a CSV that I want loaded into long-term memory. Script will probably need retries since our network is flaky. How should I structure the loading?
evals.expected_output: Batches through the bulk create API respecting the 100-records-per-call limit, supplies a deterministic client-generated id per fact so retries cannot duplicate, and inspects the created and errors arrays in the response to retry only the failures.
expectations: The output uses the bulk long-term memory creation call rather than one request per fact.
The output states the limit of 100 records per bulk call and chunks the 4,000 facts accordingly.
The output supplies a client-generated id for each record.
The output explains that a stable or deterministic id makes retries idempotent so no duplicates are created.
The output inspects the response for both created ids and per-record errors.
The output retries only the failed records rather than replaying the whole batch blindly.

evals.name: organize-and-scope-search
evals.prompt: Multi-tenant agent, memories for thousands of end users in one store. Right now every long-term memory write just sets the text and nothing else, and searches are starting to return other tenants' stuff. What fields should I be setting, and how do I scope the search?
evals.expected_output: Populates ownerId for per-user scoping plus namespace, topics and memoryType at write time, and filters searches by owner so results cannot cross tenants, explaining these structured fields exist to scope retrieval.
expectations: The output identifies the owner id field as the correct way to scope memories to an individual end user.
The output recommends setting namespace as a logical bucket within the store.
The output recommends setting topics as categorical labels.
The output recommends setting memory type and distinguishes at least two of semantic, episodic, and message.
The output filters the search call by owner so results cannot leak across tenants.
The output explains that these fields exist to scope and sharpen search rather than being decorative metadata.

evals.name: typescript-session-retrieval
evals.prompt: Our agent is TypeScript. I need to rebuild the working context when a user resumes a chat - pull back what was said in that session so far. What package and call do I use, and how does this differ from the semantic search over long-term memory?
evals.expected_output: Uses the @redis-iris/agent-memory package and the session retrieval call to fetch the ordered events for a session id, contrasting that with semantic long-term memory search across sessions.
expectations: The output installs or imports the @redis-iris/agent-memory TypeScript package.
The output uses the AgentMemory client with camelCase method naming for TypeScript.
The output retrieves the session's events by session id to rebuild working context.
The output explains that session retrieval returns the ordered raw conversation for one session.
The output contrasts this with long-term memory search, which is semantic and spans sessions.
The output does not use the Python snake_case method names for the TypeScript example.
